$comment: Copy to addressium.config.json (gitignored) before `cdk deploy`. These bootstrap the SHARED control plane. `cdk deploy` creates the admin Cognito pool and seeds each adminEmail as a user — Cognito emails them a temporary-password invite so someone can actually sign in. After first login, invite the rest of the team from the console. Per-org subscriber pools are NOT set here; they're created (or linked to an existing pool) when you Add an organization.
_stage: one of: dev | staging | prod — validated at synth (#190). It decides termination protection and log retention, so a typo is a production stack configured as a scratch one.
$comment_confirm: REQUIRED IN PRACTICE. Where subscriber confirmation links point, e.g. https://d1234.cloudfront.net/confirm (the PublicSiteUrl stack output, plus /confirm). Leave it unset and the stack falls back to https://your-site.example/confirm: signup succeeds, the mail sends, and every confirmation link goes to a domain nobody owns — double opt-in breaks with no error anywhere.
$comment_domains: Optional branded SPA hostnames are omitted here. Add adminCustomDomain and/or publicCustomDomain objects with only domainName, then deploy in us-east-1. Addressium requests the ACM certificate but never writes DNS: copy ACM's validation CNAME and the Admin/PublicCloudFrontTarget outputs into Cloudflare after the hostname choice is final.
$comment_alerts: Where infrastructure alarms go (DLQ depth, queue age, Lambda errors/throttles, DynamoDB throttles). Set opsAlertTopicArn to an SNS topic you already own — alert routing is your infrastructure, not ours. If you have no topic yet, set opsAlertEmail instead and addressium will create one and subscribe that address. Set NEITHER and every alarm fires into a void: `npm run deploy:check` will warn you.
$comment_admin_email: FROM address for admin invites and password resets. Its domain must ALREADY be a verified SES identity in this region or the deploy fails — so leave it empty on a first deploy, verify a domain, then set it and deploy again. Empty means Cognito's own sender, which is capped at 50 emails/day account-wide, sends from a shared amazonses.com address, and reports nothing about delivery: a console invite that never arrives looks identical to one that was never sent.
$comment_waf: addressium does NOT create WAF WebACLs — a resource carries only one, so ours would displace yours and silently reattach on every deploy. Create your own (REGIONAL for the API, CLOUDFRONT-scope in us-east-1 for the SPAs), attach them to the ApiStageArn / AdminDistributionId / PublicDistributionId stack outputs, and record the ARNs here. `npm run deploy:check` warns when these are unset.
$comment_sendrate: REQUIRED. This stack's share of the account SES send rate, messages/sec. Read your account quota with: aws sesv2 get-account --query 'SendQuota.MaxSendRate'. A fresh production account is 14/s; a sandbox account is 1/s. If another sender shares this account, set your share rather than the account maximum. The stack applies a 0.85 headroom factor and derives the send chunk size from it.
